app.title: AstroClassify — SDSS Astronomical Object Classification Dashboard
app.summary: A person enters one object's five photometric band magnitudes and its redshift, or loads a random observation from a labelled sample. A trained classifier then predicts the object's class and shows how confident it is. The person reads the object's magnitudes across the bands as a spectral profile, and can choose which bands to show. They then place the object on a color-color diagram, with color indices they choose, among a few thousand labelled reference objects coloured by class, to see whether the prediction fits where the object sits.

task.text: Classify a single observed object as one of a few known classes with a trained model, and check the call against where labelled reference objects fall.

data.text: A catalogue of observed objects, each with brightness in five photometric bands, a redshift and a known class, plus the measurements of one object being classified.
data.item: one observed object with five band magnitudes and a redshift

stage.text: trying out a trained classifier on individual observations, after the model is trained

mechanism.text: Number fields in the sidebar hold the object's measurements, and every change re-runs the classifier. The result card, the band-profile line chart and the color-color scatter all redraw at once in the predicted class's colour, and the scatter marks the object with a cross among reference points coloured by class.

field.text: photometric classification of stars, galaxies and quasars with machine learning in astronomy

workflow.name: classify one item with a trained model and place it among labelled examples

steps.here: Type the u, g, r, i and z magnitudes and the redshift into sidebar number fields, or press 'Load Random Observation' to fill them from a labelled sample file.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: A stored random-forest model predicts GALAXY, QSO or STAR from the six inputs. A card shows the class and the model's confidence as a percentage, with an accent in the class colour.
A spectral energy distribution chart plots apparent magnitude against the five filters on a reversed axis. A multiselect chooses which bands appear.

steps.step: compare the item against labelled reference items
steps.here: Choose X and Y color indices (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) from two dropdowns, then see the object's computed colors as a white cross on a scatter of 1200 sampled reference objects coloured by known class.

distinctive: The inputs are brightness in five fixed photometric bands plus a redshift, and the color indices are differences between neighbouring bands.
Brightness is plotted on a reversed magnitude axis, so brighter values sit higher.
The reference scatter is a fixed random sample of labelled objects, so the predicted class can be checked against where each true class clusters.
The two color-index dropdowns cannot pick the same index for both axes.

parts.title: Observational Parameters sidebar
parts.summary: Number fields for the five band magnitudes and the redshift of the object to classify, seeded with default values.

parts.title: Load Random Observation button
parts.summary: Fills the input fields with the measurements of a randomly drawn object from the labelled sample.

parts.title: Predicted class card
parts.summary: Runs the trained classifier on the inputs and shows the predicted class and its confidence, accented in the class colour.

parts.title: Spectral Energy Distribution
parts.summary: Plots the object's apparent magnitude across the photometric filters you choose, on a reversed magnitude axis.

parts.title: Color-Color Diagram
parts.summary: Scatters a sample of labelled reference objects by two color indices, coloured by class, and marks the current object with a cross.

parts.title: Color-index axis selectors
parts.summary: Two dropdowns choose which color indices form the X and Y axes, and the Y list leaves out the index already on X.
